findings.evidence:
`pkg/planner/core/operator/logicalop/base_logical_plan.go:81`: `BaseLogicalPlan.Equals` only whitelists `*LogicalSequence` and `*LogicalMaxOneRow`; otherwise it triggers `intest.Assert(false, "Equals should not be called directly")`.
`pkg/planner/core/operator/logicalop/hash64_equals_generated.go:1080`: generated `(*LogicalLock).Equals` calls `op.BaseLogicalPlan.Equals(&op2.BaseLogicalPlan)`.
`pkg/planner/cascades/memo/group_expr.go:96`: memo equality path calls `e.LogicalPlan.Equals(e2.LogicalPlan)`, so `LogicalLock.Equals` is reachable when memo needs to compare expressions (e.g. hash collision / dedup).
Later-history check: `upstream/master` still has the same `BaseLogicalPlan.Equals` guard and `LogicalLock.Equals` implementation (not fixed).
findings.fix: Mirror the `Hash64` guard logic in `BaseLogicalPlan.Equals` by allowing `*LogicalLock` as well (e.g. switch on `p.self.(type)` including `*LogicalLock`), or stop hashing/equality-comparing `BaseLogicalPlan` inside `LogicalLock` (remove the `hash64-equals:"true"` tag on `BaseLogicalPlan` and regenerate).
findings.impact: With internal checks enabled (`-tags=intest`/`enableassert` or `GO_FAILPOINTS=/enableInternalCheck=return(true)`), any execution path that ends up calling `LogicalLock.Equals` will panic via `BaseLogicalPlan.Equals`. This can break next-gen cascades planning for `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE/SHARE` and for UPDATE/DELETE paths that inject `LogicalLock` via `buildSelectLock`.
findings.verify:
Enable internal checks and exercise cascades memo equality involving `LogicalLock`:
- Build with `-tags=intest` or set `GO_FAILPOINTS="/enableInternalCheck=return(true)"`.
- Run a minimal unit/integration case that inserts/compares `LogicalLock` group expressions (or directly call `LogicalLock{}.Init(...).Equals(otherLock)`), ensuring no assert/panic.
findings.what: `BaseLogicalPlan.Equals` guard was not updated for `*LogicalLock` (while `Hash64` was), so generated `LogicalLock.Equals` can trigger an internal-check panic when equality is needed in cascades/memo.

subject: planner: fix select lock don't have Hash64 and Equals methods itself in next-gen mode. (#63227)
summary: Commit adds hash64/equals plumbing for next-gen cascades by introducing `pkg/parser/util.IHasher`, implementing `ast.SelectLockInfo.Hash64/Equals`, and generating `LogicalLock.Hash64/Equals`. A remaining high-risk issue is that `BaseLogicalPlan.Equals` still rejects `*LogicalLock` under internal checks, so `LogicalLock.Equals` can panic when memo equality is exercised; this is still present on `upstream/master`.
